paragraphs: Friend, here's what this chapter teaches me. Pharaoh had a plan, and it had taskmasters, bricks, and a river in it. But look at verse 12: "the more they were oppressed, the more they multiplied and flourished." (Exodus 1:12) Pharaoh kept pushing down, and God's people kept coming up, and that tells me no king's plan is bigger than what God has promised.

Now look at Shiphrah and Puah. Two midwives, no army, no power, and a king telling them what to do. The text says they "feared God and did not do as the king of Egypt had instructed." (Exodus 1:17) They put God first, and "God was good to the midwives" (Exodus 1:20), giving them "families of their own." (Exodus 1:21)

So if you're in a season where the pressure keeps piling on, hear me, baker. Hard days don't mean God has lost track of His people. And if you're ever standing where those midwives stood, small and nervous and unsure anyone will notice, God notices. This story is far from over, and I'm telling you, the One who wrote it is not worried.
